newsitem.title: USA: Five in Fla. hospital after all-night drug party.
newsitem.headline: Five in Fla. hospital after all-night drug party.

text.p: Five people, most of them teenagers, were rushed to area hospitals and 16 were arrested on drug dealing charges after a drug-laden, all-night "rave" party in central Florida, police said on Monday.

"I've never seen so much narcotic use in my life," Sheriff's Lt. Chris Whitis said of the party early Sunday, which attracted 5,000 young people from across the state. "There were people lying everywhere. You could hardly walk without falling over somebody."

Raves are the latest trend in teen parties -- all night affairs that combine pulse-pounding music, laser light shows and so-called "designer drugs." Typically, they are held after hours in nightclubs or civic buildings and are advertised as alcohol-free events.
Last month, a rave party in nearby Daytona Beach ended in the murder of a college student.

The Florida Legislature is considering whether to outlaw the parties, which make their profit from paid admissions. Tickets for the weekend rave were sold through a national computerized ticket agency for $30 each, police said.
Whitis said undercover officers arrested 16 people on suspicion of dealing such drugs as LSD, methamphetamine and Rohypnol, or "roofies," also known as the "date rape" drug.

Promoter Donald Johnson said on Monday he had acted responsibly, hiring on-premises security guards and paramedics. "I cannot say what happened outside these premises, within the parking area, because that's not our responsibility," he said.
Police said at least three of the five people in the hospital were teenagers, two of them just 16. All were treated and released from area hospitals.
